observation.location: lug root where the tongue meets the hub, all three lugs, worst on the heater side
observation.text: EXAMPLE (SYNTHETIC - not a real observation; shipped to exercise the triage pipeline). After about two months of continuous drying at 48 C with the spool standing upright, one of the three hub tongues had taken a permanent outward set and the two spool halves could be pulled apart by hand. No crack, no whitening - the lug root simply flowed.

part.part: hub tongue / lug joint (spool half A)

process.orientation_note: flange face down on the bed, tongues printed in-plane

service.environment: filament dryer, continuous, spool standing upright over the heater

observation.location: root of the detent bump where it meets the arm
observation.text: EXAMPLE (SYNTHETIC - not a real observation; shipped to exercise the triage pipeline). After roughly 2400 open/close cycles the detent bump grew a hairline crack at its root; the click is now inconsistent and the arm no longer holds the halves closed reliably. No single overload event - it appeared gradually.

part.part: detent bump on the retaining arm

process.orientation_note: flange face down on the bed; the arm lies in the layer plane

service.environment: bench, room temperature, spool opened and closed to swap refills

condition_violation.note: service temperature 70.0 °C is above PLA's softening_c 55.0 °C — the part was operated OUTSIDE its material envelope.
